page: Amazon Web Services c8gb.2xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. This instance features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz, with a single thread per core configuration. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard workloads. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests yield scores of 1707.2 and 13645.12, respectively, while Geekbench scores reach 1890.0 for single-core and 10105.0 for multi-core. The server demonstrates strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression performance at 14.48 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of tested systems. However, cryptographic operations represent a performance tradeoff, with the Passmark CPU encryption test scoring 1506.69, which falls into the bottom 25%. Large-block memory bandwidth is measured at 154.43 GB/sec for read operations and 83.05 GB/sec for write operations.

For machine learning workloads, the instance handles small-scale language models adequately, processing 544.17 tokens per second for prompts and generating 144.75 tokens per second using a 135M parameter model. Performance drops significantly on larger models, with prompt processing for a 7B parameter model falling to a poor 15.52 tokens per second. Given the compute-focused 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the absence of local storage or GPU accelerators, this instance is suited for containerized microservices, static web serving, software compilation, and lightweight database operations.
